issues.description: Condition reads backwards; rewrite as a guard on the disabled state
issues.detail: `not self.get_conf(...) and not key == Qt.Key_Tab` mixes two negations and `not ==` instead of `!=`. The data here is a boolean flag and a key code — the obvious shape is `if not enter_accepts and key != Qt.Key_Tab`. Bind the conf to a named local first; the algorithm becomes self-evident.

issues.description: get_conf called on every keystroke inside the completion popup
issues.detail: Reading the config on each keyPressEvent is wasteful and couples the hot path to the conf system. Cache the value on popup show, or subscribe to the option change. Pike's rule 2: measure — but this one is obvious without measuring: a settings lookup per keystroke is the wrong data flow.

issues.description: Branch is wedged into the middle of keyPressEvent instead of with sibling key handlers
issues.detail: The Enter/Tab acceptance logic belongs grouped with the other key dispatches at the top of keyPressEvent, not interleaved after `item = self.currentItem()`. Put the early-exit guard before the item lookup — it makes the control flow read linearly and avoids a wasted currentItem() call on the disabled path.

issues.description: Option name conflates Enter-only with Enter-and-Tab semantics
issues.detail: `use_enter_for_completions` defaults True and the tooltip says disabling leaves Tab only. The flag name reads like a positive feature toggle; a name like `accept_completion_with_enter` or pairing with an explicit Tab flag would make the data shape match the UI. Minor — but names are data too.

issues.description: Forwarding the original event to textedit may double-handle modifiers
issues.detail: On the disabled-Enter path the popup hides and replays the event to textedit.keyPressEvent. Worth confirming this doesn't fire twice when Qt also propagates the unhandled event after return. A small filter — eat or forward, not both — is the cleaner shape.

review.summary: Small, mostly well-scoped change adding a preference and a guard in the completion popup's key handler. The data structure is fine — a single boolean flag — but the call site reads awkwardly (`not X and not key == Y`) and reaches into the conf system on every keystroke instead of caching the value. The UI wiring and config default are straightforward. Fix the condition's readability, cache the conf lookup, and move the guard above the currentItem() work; the rest is SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE.
